correctness.rationale: The 32-fold tame elementary 2-cover C_B branched at six points has genus 17 by Riemann–Hurwitz. Its 15 four-point elliptic double quotients and one genus-two quotient provide an isogeny with 2-power kernel, hence an isomorphism of 5-divisible groups; f5=15−h+r and a=h+a(H). In characteristic five, Legendre λ supersingular iff λ²−λ+1=0, yielding 2 completions of any triple. Pairwise intersection of four-subsets and the 21 possible F25 sixth points reduce the shared-triple case to exact 12/6/3 h-counts; all nine cases h≥3 have invertible genus-two Hasse matrix, and the h4 choices 2,3,4 are projectively conjugate. For the no-shared-triple three-quartet configuration, complementary pairs partition six points and normalization reduces supersingularity and Hasse singularity to coprime univariate polynomials P_t(c),det_t(c) for t=α,1−α. Independent exact F25 polynomial gcd computations confirmed both gcd 1, not just sampled field points. Thus h≥3⇒r=2, h≤4, f5≥13 and a≤4. At h4 four supersingular elliptics give Newton slopes 0^13,(1/2)^8,1^13. The coprime polynomial argument is essential for the infinite algebraic closure.
